meanings.bodyweightKg: Bodyweight in kilograms; null if not measured
meanings.fatPercent: Body fat in percent; null if not measured

meanings.archived: Hidden from pickers; stays valid in history (custom exercises are archived, never deleted)
meanings.name: Exercise name
meanings.type: How sets are measured; fixed once created

meanings.agent: Name of the agent that wrote the note; null when the lifter wrote it
meanings.createdAt: Time the note was written in UTC
meanings.exerciseId: Built-in or custom exercise the note is about; a soft reference
meanings.pinned: Pinned notes show on the exercise in every workout until deleted; other notes show on it in the next workout that includes the exercise
meanings.workoutId: The workout in which the note was written; a soft reference, null when written outside a workout. Deleting the workout keeps the note

meanings.agent: Name of the agent that wrote the comment; null when the lifter wrote it
meanings.createdAt: Time the comment was written in UTC; a comment newer than the note's last showing brings the note back once
meanings.noteId: The exercise note this comment answers

meanings.effortScale: Effort scale for this routine's targets and workouts started from it; absent or null for older routines
meanings.exercises: The routine's exercises in order, each with target sets (weights in kilograms, distances in metres, durations in seconds, rep ranges as min/max, and optional RPE or reps in reserve)
meanings.folderId: The folder holding the routine; null when unfiled or the folder is gone
meanings.position: Order within its folder; lower first, ties ordered by id
meanings.title: Routine name

meanings.position: Order among folders; lower first, ties ordered by id
meanings.title: Folder name

meanings.autoUpdateRoutineValues: After a routine-based workout, copy the logged values back into the routine
meanings.countWarmups: Whether warm-up sets count toward volume, set counts and records
meanings.defaultRestSeconds: Rest timer for new exercise entries; 0 means off
meanings.distanceUnit: Unit for long distances; stored values stay in metres
meanings.firstWeekday: First day of the week, 0 = Sunday
meanings.previousValues: Where 'previous' values come from while logging: any workout or the same routine
meanings.rpeEnabled: Legacy RPE preference retained for compatibility
meanings.shortDistanceUnit: Unit for short distances; stored values stay in metres
meanings.trackRepsInReserve: Whether the app prompts for effort in the workout's scale after logging a set; null means off
meanings.weightUnit: Unit for showing and entering weight; stored values stay in kilograms

meanings.endedAt: startedAt plus the active duration; null while the workout is in progress
meanings.initialPlan: Routine title, effort scale, and ordered exercise and set targets captured at start; null when unknown or unplanned
meanings.routineId: The routine the workout was started from, if any; a soft reference
meanings.title: Workout name shown in history

meanings.doubleDumbbellVolume: Count the set weight twice in volume (one dumbbell per hand)
meanings.exerciseId: Built-in or custom exercise id; a soft reference
meanings.exerciseName: The exercise's name when logged, shown if the exercise no longer exists
meanings.exerciseType: How sets of this exercise are measured; decides which set values are used
meanings.position: Order within the workout; lower first, ties ordered by id
meanings.restSeconds: Rest timer after a set in seconds; 0 means off
meanings.supersetId: Entries of one workout sharing this number form a superset; null if none
meanings.workoutId: The workout this entry belongs to (parent)

meanings.agent: Name of the agent that wrote the note; null when the lifter wrote it
meanings.createdAt: Time the note was written in UTC
meanings.pinned: Pinned notes show in every later workout of the same routine until deleted or unpinned; other notes show in the next workout of that routine (the next workout of any kind for a workout without a routine). Only a note on a workout with a routine can be pinned
meanings.workoutId: The workout in which this note was written

meanings.agent: Name of the agent that wrote the comment; null when the lifter wrote it
meanings.createdAt: Time the comment was written in UTC; a comment newer than the note's last showing brings the note back once
meanings.noteId: The workout note this comment answers

meanings.seconds: Default rest in seconds for exercises added to this workout. Zero turns the timer off. Null uses account settings. Clear the preference by setting seconds to null; it is deleted with its workout.
meanings.workoutId: The workout to which this rest preference belongs; its record ID equals the workout ID

meanings.completedAt: When the set was ticked off (UTC); null if not completed
meanings.count: Floors or steps for those exercise types; null when unused
meanings.distanceMeters: Distance in metres; null when unused
meanings.durationSeconds: Duration in seconds; null when unused
meanings.planSlot: Zero-based exercise and set indices in the workout initial plan, independent of row order; null if unplanned or unknown
meanings.position: Order within the entry; lower first, ties ordered by id
meanings.reps: Repetitions; null when the exercise type doesn't count them
meanings.repsInReserve: Estimated additional repetitions possible when the set ended, from 0 to 10; zero means no repetitions remained, null means unrecorded
meanings.rpe: Rate of perceived exertion from 1 to 10 in half steps; null if not given
meanings.type: normal, warmup, failure or drop set
meanings.weightKg: Weight in kilograms; for weighted bodyweight the added load, for assisted bodyweight the assistance; null when the exercise type has no weight
meanings.workoutExerciseId: The exercise entry this set belongs to (parent)

rules.text: String lengths count UTF-16 code units. Timestamps are UTC with exactly three fraction digits (2026-11-10T19:57:06.000Z); other spellings are invalid, so each instant has one spelling and content compares as JSON.
rules.sizes: A record's content is at most 200000 bytes of UTF-8 JSON, measured as compact JSON with non-ASCII characters not escaped (larger content is invalid). A request body is at most 1048576 bytes; clients split uploads to stay below it. A download page stops early once its records hold about 800000 bytes, and always moves the cursor by at least one revision.
rules.restore: hello's restoredFrom names the lineage a restored backup belonged to and the backup's revision; revisions up to it mean the same in that lineage and the current one. It is informational: a device that sees a new lineage resets, confirms identical copies by offering them again, and gives every other difference to the user for review.
rules.lineage: Push and pull carry the lineage from hello. A different lineage, or a pull cursor beyond the account's revision, is answered cursor_reset; in the second case the server first gives the account a new lineage.
rules.push: Each submission is decided on its own, in request order; the answer has exactly one result per submission, in the same order. Submission ids are unique within a request.
rules.put: baseRevision is the revision the edit started from, null to create. Content holds every field of the release; null means not set. Fields the release doesn't define keep their stored values.
rules.delete: baseRevision is the revision deleted, or null when the deleter has no copy (accepted only if the server has no live record). descendants lists every live record below it with the revision the deleter knows; any difference is stale. Deleting removes all descendants. The server checks all descendants, including kinds outside the requesting release. Singleton kinds cannot be deleted. A shared-ID child can be cleared by updating its content. A separate deletion of that child is refused while its owner is live. During recovery, retry a missing or deleted child's marker after a missing owner arrives. Accept that marker when its same-ID owner is deleted. Other deleted or unknown records accept deletion.
rules.accepted: The change is stored at revision; also answered for a repeat of an accepted submission id with the same content (the original revision), and when the content already equals the current copy.
rules.conflict: stale: the record changed since the base (or a descendant differs). deleted: the record is deleted. exists: a create of an id that exists with other content. parent_deleted: the parent is deleted. current is the server's copy for the requester's release, or null when the record never existed.
rules.retry_later: parent_missing: the parent isn't on the server yet; send again after it.
rules.invalid: invalid_content: the content breaks the release's rules. submission_reused: the id was used before for a different change (receipts are kept for 90 days). not_singleton: a singleton kind under another id. not_deletable: a delete of a singleton or an independent delete of a shared-ID child outside recovery.
rules.pull: Changes after cursor in revision order. limit defaults to 100 (at most 500); waitMs (default 0, at most 25000) waits for a first change. Kinds the release doesn't have are skipped. A record the release can't represent is sent as unavailable. Save the page's cursor together with its changes.
rules.errors: invalid_request (HTTP 400): malformed request. unauthorized (401). unsupported_release (400): the server doesn't accept this release; serverReleases lists those it does. update_required (426): no common release; update names the side to update. cursor_reset (409): download everything again after connecting. unavailable (503): try again later.
